correctness.rationale: For \(V=\mathbb F_2^n/C\), the coordinate syndrome classes are nonzero and pairwise distinct exactly because \(d(C)\ge3\), and they span \(V\). Any degree-one realization gives a scalar check map with kernel \(C\), hence a unique injection \(V\hookrightarrow\mathbb F_{2^M}\). Conversely, any injection maps the coordinate syndrome classes to nonzero distinct coefficients, whose inverses and an arbitrary anchor give a distinct admissible support with exactly kernel \(C\). The constructions are inverse. Counting ordered independent images of a basis gives the product formula, and exhaustive finite-field replay checks the correspondence.

originality.rationale: The September 2026 primary source proves existence and the minimum extension degree but does not parameterize or enumerate all representations. The accepted theorem identifies the complete representation space with injections from the intrinsic syndrome quotient and obtains a universal exact count. Older Goppa enumeration papers count equivalence classes of irreducible or extended irreducible Goppa codes, a different object. Semantic research-record and public searches under degree-one, support, quotient, minimal-field, and representation-count terminology found no covering statement.

value.rationale: The primary source newly shows that every binary distance-three-or-better code can be represented as a degree-one Goppa code, but existence alone leaves substantial nonuniqueness. The accepted result resolves that nonuniqueness completely by giving an intrinsic syndrome-space parameterization and an exact count over every allowable extension field. The universality of the count, depending only on redundancy, is useful for support synthesis, random realization generation, and equivalence or security analyses.
